thread:
maya: Quick q — where should the canary decision live: edge LB (per-request) or a central controller? We need strong session affinity for KV cache warmup and an automatic fallback path if the canary starts degrading. Any tradeoffs I should call out?

omar: My 2c: central controller for decisioning makes rollbacks simpler and gives us a single place to evaluate signals. But it increases coupling and adds a control-plane dependency at request time.

liz: Agree with omar. Also consider what 'affinity' means for us: sticky routing to the canary instance vs sticky session semantics for a user across variants. Those are different and have different failure modes.

kevin: Edge decision reduces request-hop latency and avoids a live dependency on the control plane, but then every edge needs the same logic + signal set. Ops burden goes up. For warmup you could do prefix pre-warming from control plane either way.

maya: Right — the warmup concern is real. If we switch traffic live to canary and haven’t primed KV / attention caches, p99 spikes. We were thinking to backfill warmup via a shadowing job, but need affinity so a user keeps hitting warmed hosts.

emily: From SRE side, automatic fallback must be able to do at least two things: (1) fail traffic back to baseline model, (2) degrade to a lower-cost but lower-quality variant in the same pool. Which fallback wins? region first or variant first?

liz: Proposal: fallback precedence = same-region baseline -> cross-region baseline -> lower-tier variant. Keeps latency stable for most cases. We should make precedence configurable by tenant.

omar: One architectural pattern that helped elsewhere: control-plane issues are mitigated by a short-lived signed token distributed to edge. Token encodes active rollout buckets + TTL. Edge makes final decision using the token; control plane rotates it when signals change. So we get centralized policy + edge resilience.

kevin: Example token payload (pseudo):
```
{
  "route_version": "v12",
  "buckets": ["10%","90%"],
  "sticky_window": 3600,
  "sig": "..."
}
```
Edge verifies sig and applies bucket logic. If token expires, edge falls back to baseline.

maya: That looks promising. A couple followups: how do we ensure token rotation latency isn't a blindspot? If control plane decides to rollback, edges must pick up new token ASAP.

emily: We can push rotation via a pub/sub invalidation channel (region-local) + expiry fallback. Invalidation gets accepted best-effort; expiry is the safety net.

liz: Also need to think about observability. The token should carry a rollout_id so traces can correlate canary traffic. Probe events must include warmed_cache=true/false and probe latency. We can use those to gate rollouts.

omar: Agree. For gating, central controller should emit a single scalar 'canary_health' computed from: error_rate, tail_latency, warmed_cache_ratio, model-quality-regen. Edges don't need to compute gate, just send probe telemetry.

kevin: One more ops note: if we require session affinity for warm caches, then doubling capacity at canary to accept warm-only traffic is expensive. Alternative: cooperative cache warmup where warm hosts accept shadowed traffic to warm but mark responses as shadowed so clients don't observe it.

maya: So action items:
- test token-based decision prototype (omar)
- define probe schema + rollout_id in traces (liz + emily)
- investigate shadow warmup cost model (kevin + maya)

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: canary-token-proto -> staging (build #1225). ETA ~15m. :rocket:

omar: I'll PR a prototype for token format + verification helper this week. One design question: should token include a TTL only or absolute expiry + revision id? I prefer absolute expiry + revision so we can reason about staleness.

liz: Absolute expiry + revision sounds safer. Also include 'fallback_policy' shorthand so edges can precompute fallback without extra lookups.

emily: For rollbacks triggered by ops, let's make sure we have a manual kill switch in the control plane that immediately rotates tokens to baseline and publishes invalidation. Ops runbook will need steps and an SLA for token propagation.

maya: Thanks all — this gives a path forward. I'll sketch a small RFC for the token approach + the probe schema and tag owners for the followups.

kevin: Ping me on the cost model once you have the shadowing numbers. I can run a quick sim.

liz: Nice incremental plan. If we keep the edge decision cheap (sig verify + bucket hash) we get most benefits without a heavy control-plane RPC on every request.

maya: Cool. I'll create the RFC draft and post here. Shelving deep quality gating math until we have probe telemetry in staging. :thumbsup:
